record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: Regard the quantum capacity of a noisy quantum channel as a function on the space of channels. Is this function continuous, for example with respect to the completely bounded norm: whenever two channels are close in channel distance, must their quantum capacities also be close?

evidence.quote: The quantum capacity of a noisy quantum channel can be regarded as a function on the space of all channels. Is this function continuous? In other words: If the distance (e.g. with respect to the cb-norm) between two channels is small, is the distance between the corresponding capacities small as well?
In [1] it was shown that the quantum capacity as a function of the channel is lower semi-continuous.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and let $\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$ denote the set of completely positive trace-preserving linear maps (quantum channels) from operators on $\mathcal{H}_A$ to operators on $\mathcal{H}_B$. For a channel $\mathcal{N}\in\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$, the coherent information for an input state $\rho$ is
$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal{N}) := S(\mathcal{N}(\rho)) - S((\mathcal{N}\otimes\mathrm{id})(|\psi_\rho\rangle\langle\psi_\rho|)),$$
where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy and $|\psi_\rho\rangle$ is any purification of $\rho$. The quantum capacity of $\mathcal{N}$ is defined by the regularized formula
$$Q(\mathcal{N}) := \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\max_{\rho^{(n)}}I_c(\rho^{(n)},\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}).$$
On the set of channels, equip $\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$ with the completely bounded norm distance $\|\mathcal{N}_1-\mathcal{N}_2\|_{cb}$.

Question: Is the map $\mathcal{N}\mapsto Q(\mathcal{N})$ continuous with respect to the cb-norm? Equivalently, for every $\varepsilon>0$ does there exist $\delta>0$ such that whenever $\|\mathcal{N}_1-\mathcal{N}_2\|_{cb}<\delta$ one has $|Q(\mathcal{N}_1)-Q(\mathcal{N}_2)|<\varepsilon$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is essentially solved. Leung and Smith (2009, "Continuity of Quantum Channel Capacities", Commun. Math. Phys.) proved that the classical, quantum, and private classical capacities are continuous in the diamond/cb-norm on finite-dimensional channels, with explicit continuity bounds depending on the output dimension. Subsequent refined continuity bounds were given by Shirokov, Leditzky and others (tight bounds, energy-constrained versions). The Open Quantum Problems entry lists the problem's status as solved.

status_evidence.title: Continuity of Quantum Channel Capacities
status_evidence.snippet: Leung and Smith prove that classical, quantum and private classical capacities are continuous with respect to the diamond norm, with bounded variation in terms of epsilon and output dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum capacity is continuous in the diamond (cb) norm on finite-dimensional channels.

status_evidence.title: Continuity of the Quantum channel capacity – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Status: Solved. The continuity problem was resolved by Leung and Smith (2009).
status_evidence.claim: The open problem is recorded as solved.

status_evidence.title: Tight continuity bounds for capacities of quantum channels
status_evidence.snippet: Shirokov obtains tight continuity bounds for capacities of quantum channels.
status_evidence.claim: Refined tight continuity bounds have been established.
